attribution: E‑E‑A‑T + CITE content-quality rubric adapted from the MIT-licensed AgriciDaniel/claude-seo (E‑E‑A‑T audit, QRG-aligned) and seranking/seo-skills (60-item E‑E‑A‑T + 30-item CITE content audit). Scoped to signals extractable from a single fetched page plus Claude's per-factor judgement. See docs/omi/seo-skills-integration-plan.md, Integration A.

categories.label: Experience
categories.description: First-hand experience with the subject — original research, case studies, own photography, hands-on testing, lived detail. QRG's first 'E'.
checks: Signals of first-hand use (tested / measured / visited / built it)
Specific detail only a practitioner would include

categories.label: Expertise
categories.description: Demonstrated topical depth and a credible, named author with relevant standing (knowsAbout).
checks: Named author with relevant credentials / bio
Depth proportional to the query's difficulty (YMYL held to a higher bar)

categories.label: Authoritativeness
categories.description: Recognised as a go-to source — external citations to authoritative sources, brand/entity presence, corroboration.
checks: Brand/entity is a recognised voice on the topic

categories.label: Trust
categories.description: The most heavily weighted factor (QRG). Accuracy, transparency, and safety signals: HTTPS, contactability, clear authorship, dates, corrections.
checks: Accurate, honest, non-deceptive; transparent about sources and limitations

categories.label: Citation readiness (CITE)
categories.description: How quotable the page is to AI answer engines: self-contained answer passages, question-shaped headings, attributed stats, citation-to-claim density.
checks: Self-contained answer passages (~130–170 words) an engine can lift
Attributed statistics and a healthy citation-to-claim ratio

signals.note: Objective, deterministically-detected page signals handed to Claude and shown to the AM as evidence. They inform the per-factor grades rather than scoring separately.
